title: 7-round AES-192: schedule-optimized whole-key headline

target.description: The author's attack-level claim for7-round AES-192, with standard left ShiftRows, initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The explicit selected-subkey procedure is separately catalogued as aes192-7r-functions-minier2005-schedule-optimized-selected-subkeys. Section5.4 reduces the second-half k_tau2 search from ten bytes to eight by using the standard AES-192 key schedule.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key or known-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: A 2^32 chosen-plaintext structure varying four initial bytes with the other twelve fixed.
assumptions: A random32-bit model for the four internal parameters supports the birthday estimate. Sixteen-value preliminary matches are checked over all256 y values.

This record preserves the complete-cipher attack headline. Master-key completion is not separately reconstructed or priced in this paper; GM00's round-peeling argument is discussed in the audit, not silently added to this budget.

time.reported: Smaller second-half search:8 guessed bytes instead of10; total work not restated
time.note: The first-half table still enumerates10 bytes. The text does not give a new total exponent, so2^144 is not automatically reduced by16.

data.note: One four-byte structure, reused throughout the search.

memory.reported: Split tables with altered second-half search; whole peak not restated
memory.note: Section5.4 does not provide a new peak-storage estimate.

preprocessing.reported: Ciphertext-dependent per-kini/per-c-pair tables inside the search
preprocessing.note: No independent complete preprocessing budget is separately stated.

success.description: No separate numerical success is stated for the AES192 schedule-optimized endpoint. Section5.4 changes the second-half enumeration from ten to eight bytes without restating joint success, total work or peak memory. Retain the Section5.3 half-probability only as an upstream baseline collision event, not as an adapted-endpoint or complete-key guarantee.

components.description: Section5.3 BASELINE split search: a random2^16 sample among2^32 internal function descriptions gives about one-half collision probability and supplies kini,k_tau1,k_tau2 under the source model. Section5.4 reduces the second-half key enumeration from ten to eight bytes, but does not separately quantify success of that schedule-constrained adaptation.
